title: Squalene Quantification using Nile Red Staining
author: Sebastian ST Triesch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.y6vfze6

steps.title: Prepare and Adjust Culture
steps.instruction: Adjust the Synechocystis culture to a specific optical density and split into two portions.

substeps.instruction: Measure the OD at 750 nm of 1-2 ml Synechocystis culture.
Adjust the culture to 2 ml of OD (750 nm) = 0.2 in BG-11 media.
Split the adjusted culture into two 1 ml portions: one for Nile Red staining and one as a negative control.

steps.title: Stain with Nile Red
steps.instruction: Stain the designated culture portion with Nile Red, ensuring proper PPE is worn due to DMSO.

substeps.instruction: Add Nile Red to one 1 ml portion to a final concentration of 10 µg/ml.
Wear gloves and a lab coat to prevent DMSO from staining skin and cloth.

steps.title: Incubate Samples
steps.instruction: Incubate the cultures for 30 minutes in the dark.

steps.title: Centrifuge and Wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the samples and remove the supernatant.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge all samples for 5 min at 5000 xg.
Carefully pipette out and discard the supernatant, avoiding resuspension of the pellet or loss of cells.

steps.title: Resuspend Pellets
steps.instruction: Thoroughly resuspend all pellets in 1 ml BG-11 media.

steps.title: Prepare 96-Well Plate
steps.instruction: Distribute the resuspended samples into a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Fill wells with 200 µl per well.
Ensure sample volume allows for four wells per sample.

steps.title: Measure Optical Density
steps.instruction: Measure the OD(750 nm) of each well using a plate reader.

steps.title: Measure Fluorescence
steps.instruction: Measure Nile Red fluorescence using specific wavelengths.

steps.title: Analyze Data
steps.instruction: Normalize and compare the fluorescence data.

substeps.instruction: Normalize each well's fluorescence to its respective OD.
Subtract the fluorescence of the negative control (without Nile Red) from the fluorescence of the stained sample.
Compare results to wild type Nile Red stained fluorescence.
